title: MARIO: A Superadditive Multi-Algorithm Interworking Optimization Framework for Analog Circuit Sizing
problem: Analog circuit sizing involves expensive simulations, non-linearity, and high dimensionality; diverse circuit types have different optimization landscapes, making single-algorithm approaches sub-optimal.
motivation: Analog design automation requires robust optimization, but no single algorithm excels across all circuit families. Multi-algorithm portfolios could achieve better results through dynamic adaptation.
method: MARIO combines a pool of optimization algorithms via multi-algorithm interworking protocol achieving superadditivity. Uses multitask Gaussian process regression and portfolio optimization for online resource reallocation. Includes evaluation data broadcast for cross-algorithm cooperation and asynchronous parallelization for algorithms with different computational costs.
key_novelty: Multi-algorithm interworking framework achieving superadditive optimization by dynamically adapting algorithm allocation based on progress and cost.
contributions: Achieves optimization superadditivity over individual member algorithms
Flexible online adaptation of member algorithms via resource reallocation
Superior performance vs. state-of-the-art algorithm-combining tools

metrics.other: superadditive optimization performance improvement (values not specified)

limitations: Not discussed; specific circuit families tested, convergence guarantees, and scalability to extremely large designs unclear.
primary_theme: Multi-algorithm framework for analog circuit sizing
